from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines_text = ["Find roots by solving f(x) = 0.", "Use linear approximation with tangent lines.", "Tangent line slope reveals the root.", "The tangent hits the x-axis closer.", "Repeat to hone in on roots."]
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisite: The Tangent Line Intuition", lecture_lines_text)

        # Define Axes
        axes = Axes(
            x_range=[-1, 5, 1], y_range=[-1, 3, 1],
            axis_config={"include_tip": False}
        ).scale(0.6)
        self.place_in_area(axes, "B1", "E5")
        self.add(axes)

        # Function f(x)
        func = axes.plot(lambda x: 0.2*(x-1)*(x-4) + 1, x_range=[0, 4.5])
        self.add(func)

        # Animation Elements
        x0 = 3.5
        y0 = 0.2*(x0-1)*(x0-4) + 1
        dot_x0 = Dot(axes.c2p(x0, y0), color="#FF9900")
        tangent = Line(axes.c2p(0, 1.5), axes.c2p(4.5, -0.5), color="#FFFFFF")
        x1 = 4.1
        dot_x1 = Dot(axes.c2p(x1, 0), color="#00FF00")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(BLUE)
        self.play(Create(axes), Create(func))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(BLUE)
        self.play(Create(tangent))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FF9900")
        self.play(Create(dot_x0))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[3].set_color("#00FF00")
        self.play(Create(dot_x1))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.lecture[3].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[4].set_color(BLUE)
        self.wait(1)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Formulate the Newton-Raphson iterative step.",
            "x_{n+1} equals x_n minus f/f'.",
            "Refine estimates with each iteration.",
            "Starts must be close enough.",
            "Automatically converge on the solution."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Newton-Raphson Iteration", lecture_lines)
        
        # Assets
        formula = MathTex("x_{n+1} = x_n - \\frac{f(x_n)}{f'(x_n)}", color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(formula, "B2", scale_factor=1.5)
        
        dot = Dot(color=BLUE)
        dot.move_to(self.grid["D2"])
        self.add(dot)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        self.play(Write(formula))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        self.play(Indicate(formula))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        dot2 = Dot(color=YELLOW).move_to(self.grid["D3"])
        self.play(dot.animate.move_to(dot2), run_time=1.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(RED))
        warning = Text("!", color=RED, font_size=40).next_to(formula, RIGHT)
        self.play(FadeIn(warning))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color(GREEN))
        dot3 = Dot(color=GREEN).move_to(self.grid["D4"])
        self.play(dot.animate.move_to(dot3), run_time=1.5)
        self.wait(1)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Extend root finding to complex numbers.",
            "Polynomials like z^3-1 have roots.",
            "Which root will z_0 reach?"
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Transitioning to Complex Planes", lecture_lines)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Extend root finding to complex numbers.
        grid = ComplexPlane().add_coordinates()
        grid.set_stroke(color="#444444", width=1)
        self.place_in_area(grid, "A1", "F6", scale_factor=0.6)
        self.play(Create(grid))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#444444")
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Polynomials like z^3-1 have roots.
        formula = MathTex("f(z) = z^3 - 1").set_color("#FFFFFF")
        self.place_at_grid(formula, "B3", scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(Write(formula))
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FFFFFF")
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Which root will z_0 reach?
        z0 = Dot(point=self.grid["E2"], color="#FF00FF")
        z0_label = MathTex("z_0").next_to(z0, UP).set_color("#FF00FF")
        target = Dot(point=self.grid["C5"], color="#00FFFF")
        target_label = Text("root", font_size=24).next_to(target, DOWN).set_color("#00FFFF")
        
        path = CurvedArrow(z0.get_center(), target.get_center(), angle=-TAU/8)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(z0), Write(z0_label))
        self.play(Create(path))
        self.play(FadeIn(target), Write(target_label))
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#00FFFF")
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: Newton's Method and the Beauty of Newton Fractals
outline.target_audience: Undergraduate students in mathematics or computer science

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Tangent Line Intuition
sections.content: Briefly explain the goal of root-finding: solving f(x) = 0. Introduce the concept of a linear approximation using the tangent line. Visualize a curve f(x) and show how a tangent line at a guess point x_0 intersects the x-axis at a closer point x_1.
sections.example: Imagine a drone trying to land on a target (root) on uneven terrain (the curve); the drone uses its current angle (tangent) to predict where the ground will hit zero.

sections.title: The Newton-Raphson Iteration
sections.content: Formalize the geometric intuition into the iterative formula: x_{n+1} = x_n - f(x_n)/f'(x_n). Emphasize that each step refines the estimate. Mention conditions for convergence (starting close enough to the root).
sections.example: A 'smart' archery game where every time you miss, the game calculates the derivative of your error to adjust your next arrow's aim automatically until you hit the bullseye.

sections.title: Transitioning to Complex Planes
sections.content: Extend the domain from real numbers to complex numbers (z = x + iy). Explain that for a polynomial like f(z) = z^3 - 1, there are three possible roots (complex numbers). The question becomes: which root does a starting point z_0 converge to?
sections.example: Three different colored magnetic poles (the roots) placed on a table; a metal ball (z_0) is released; which pole will it eventually be pulled into?

sections.title: The Emergence of Newton Fractals
sections.content: Describe the coloring process: assign a color to each root. For every pixel (z_0) on a 2D plane, calculate which root the Newton iteration converges to and color the pixel accordingly. The boundaries between these 'basins of attraction' create infinitely complex, self-similar patterns.
sections.example: A digital map where the border between the 'influence zones' of three different kingdoms turns out to be a jagged, fractal coastline, no matter how much you zoom in.

sections.title: Summary and Visual Synthesis
sections.content: Conclude by connecting the simple algebraic rule to the chaotic beauty of the fractal. Summarize: Simple Iteration + Complex Domain = Infinite Complexity.
sections.example: Show a 5-second animation morphing from a simple tangent line graph to a fully rendered Newton Fractal, illustrating the transition from calculus to chaotic art.
